hint: You can paste a secret reference instead of the secret, like op://vault/item/field or vault://secret/app#password. It is fetched from your secret source when connecting.
title: Secret sources
description: External password managers Termix reads secrets from when you connect: 1Password Connect, Infisical, Bitwarden Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, or Bitwarden and Vaultwarden through bw serve. Tokens are stored encrypted on the server and never sent back to the browser.
tokenKeep: Leave empty to keep the current token

referenceStatus.invalid: This is not a valid secret reference.
referenceStatus.no_source: No secret source is set up for this type of reference.
referenceStatus.not_found: {{source}} has no secret at this reference.
referenceStatus.denied: {{source}} refused access to this secret. Check the token and its permissions.

required: Name, server URL and the login details are required

privateEndpoints.label: Private endpoint allowlist
privateEndpoints.description: Private or loopback hosts a secret source may reach, one per line. A self-hosted server, like 1Password Connect, Vault or bw serve, usually needs its own address listed here.

plugin.name: Secret Sources
plugin.description: Pull host passwords and keys from 1Password, Bitwarden, Infisical, HashiCorp Vault, KeePass, AWS, Azure or Google Cloud when you connect instead of storing them in Termix.

kinds.bitwarden-vault: Bitwarden or Vaultwarden (each user signs in)

kindHints.infisical: Uses a machine identity with Universal Auth. Reference:
kindHints.bitwarden-sm: Leave the URL as is for bitwarden.com, or use your own server's address. Reference:
kindHints.bitwarden-cli: Run bw serve where Termix can reach it and keep the vault unlocked. Field is username, password, totp, notes, uri or a custom field name. Reference:
kindHints.keepass: Termix downloads the file from this address, like a WebDAV or Nextcloud link, and opens it with the master password. Field is Password unless you add #UserName, #URL, #Notes or a custom field. Reference:
kindHints.aws-secrets-manager: Use an access key of an IAM user or role allowed secretsmanager:GetSecretValue and ListSecrets. Add #key to read one key of a JSON secret. Reference:
kindHints.azure-key-vault: Use an app registration with a client secret that may get and list secrets in this vault. Add /version to pin a version. Reference:
kindHints.gcp-secret-manager: Use a service account key with the Secret Manager Secret Accessor role. Add /version to pin a version, latest otherwise. Reference:
kindHints.bitwarden-vault: Each user unlocks their own vault with SSO, email or a personal API key, plus their master password, and sees only what their account can. Session length is in hours (8 if empty). The SSO identifier is your organization identifier, if your server asks for one. Field is username, password, totp, notes, uri, privatekey or a custom field name. Reference:

picker.failed: Could not list the items. Check that the vault is unlocked.
picker.noSources: Add a Bitwarden or Vaultwarden (bw serve) source to pick items from it.

unlock.title: Unlock vault
unlock.intro: Sign in to your own account. Your vault stays unlocked for you only, until the session ends.
unlock.ssoHint: Sign in in the new window.
unlock.ssoPaste: When the window shows a page that can't load, copy its address and paste it below.
unlock.retry: Unlocked. Connect to the host again.
unlock.noneHint: Ask an admin to add a Bitwarden or Vaultwarden source where each user signs in.
